subject: Multiple imputation not robust after dropping markers

messages.author: ef49ed6122073bff
messages.subject: Multiple imputation not robust after dropping markers
parts:
Hi,

I have a question about the performance of multiple imputation in a low marker density region of the map. I have previously done QTL mapping in one family using standard interval mapping, hk, multiple imputation and multiple QTL mapping with missing genotype filled by multiple imputation. These methods indicate a QTL at the same location (specific locations differ by only 0.2 cM in the map between genotype probability-based methods and imp-based methods). The location is also consistent with mapping results from another replicate. 

I am now running mapping using a less dense version of the map that contain only markers shared with another replicates in the same family. The markers within the 1.5-LOD confidence interval of the QTL are all still present in the map, but a large number of markers before the left boundary of the CI were dropped, creating a gap in that part of the map. Rerunning mapping using SIM and HK indicates a QTL at the same location as in the denser map. However, when I run multiple imputation or MQM, the QTL location shifted to inside the gap, i.e., outside the 1.5-LOD confidence interval from mapping with the denser map, and would have been among the group of markers that were dropped from the map. Multiple imputation and MQM agrees on the peak location. So it seems that after a group of markers are dropped from the map, discrepancy appears between genotype probability-based methods and multiple imputation-based methods. The former indicate QTL consistent with the location before markers were dropped,but the latter indicates a QTL inside the gap created by the dropped markers. This location is never before indicated in any family with any mapping method so we are skeptical of this result. I have repeated the analysis with imputations up to 10,000 times and got the same result. There aren't a lot of missing genotype in the region. No selective genotyping was used. 

I read in the R/qtl book that SIM is not robust, especially when marker density is low, and that multiple imputation is supposed to be much more robust. This, however, seems to be the opposite of what I observed. I'm wondering if there is an explanation of why the the peak location shifted to the middle of the gap and with this less dense map, which result should I trust.

Many thanks!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Multiple imputation not robust after dropping markers
parts:
I can understand your concern, but it's hard for me to tell what's going on, and whether this should be a general concern, without further details. The results go against my general experience. I wonder whether you've done sufficient imputations to deal with the missing genotype information. If you re-run sim.geno and then scanone with method="imp", do you consistently get the same answer, and with evidence for a QTL in the region with no markers? That would be surprising to me.

I'd recommend against omitting markers and focusing on only those that are present across multiple populations. I always want more genotype information rather than less.

karl

messages.author: ef49ed6122073bff
messages.subject: Re: Multiple imputation not robust after dropping markers
parts:
Hi Karl,

Here are some updates.

I did multiple imputation for 8192, 10000, 20000 and 30000 times and ran scanone with imp, I consistently got the same result, which places the QTL in the gap. 

I then added those markers I dropped in the gap region back and rerun multiple imputation with everything else being the same, the QTL moved back to the position that is consistent with all other analyses. This suggests to me that the gap is creating a problem for multiple imputation for some reason. I wanted to compare the simulated genotypes vs the real genotypes in the gap region but the pull.draws was too big, the txt file I direct it to never finished to be written.

Thank you for the advice for noting dropping markers when I do have genotype data. I agree that this is the right thing to do.

Mingzi
